articles.title: Road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu highlight dangers of road conflicts
articles.summary: Several road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu City recently involved physical violence, one even involving an eight-year-old girl who was injured after an object was thrown into the tricycle she was…

blocks.text: Several road rage incidents in Rizal and Cebu City recently involved physical violence, one even involving an eight-year-old girl who was injured after an object was thrown into the tricycle she was riding.
In Rizal, the child was reportedly hit in the head after her mother got into an argument with a motorcycle rider at a tricycle terminal.
In Cebu City, separate incidents involved a pickup driver allegedly chasing a motorcycle passenger with a knife and a group of motorcycle riders attacking another rider.

According to “Kapuso Mo, Jessica Soho,” the incidents highlight how arguments on the road can escalate, with authorities and experts discussing the possible legal, physical, and psychological consequences of such confrontations.
Girl injured after being hit by object
On September 21, Analyn and her eight-year-old daughter, ‘Joyce’, were on their way home in Rizal when they got into an argument with a motorcycle rider at a tricycle terminal.
Analyn said the motorcycle was blocking the tricycle they were about to ride. She said her daughter politely asked the rider to move, but the man responded angrily.
The argument ended when Analyn and her daughter boarded the tricycle. However, she said the motorcycle rider and his female companion followed them.
Analyn said the pair continued recording and shouting at them before an object was thrown into their tricycle.
The object hit Joyce in the head, causing a wound that required three stitches. A doctor said ‘Joyce’ suffered a three-centimeter lacerated wound on the right side of her forehead.

A psychologist who assessed ‘Joyce’ said she showed anxiety and hyperarousal, as well as behavioral changes after the incident. The psychologist said returning to a regular routine, including going back to school, may help reduce the child's trauma.
Police identify motorcycle rider
Police identified the motorcycle rider as Jayvee Aduque, an alleged online seller of motorcycle spare parts. His passenger was identified as his partner, Shyrie Recto Morta.
KMJS went to their rented home in Antipolo to seek their side, but the two were not there. Their landlord said their belongings were still at the property.
A barangay official said Aduque and Morta had no record in their barangay, while police said the two had indicated that they would surrender but had not appeared at the station.

Police said Aduque may face a physical injury complaint over the incident involving Joyce. Depending on the classification of the injury, the possible penalties range from days to years of imprisonment.
Police also said the motorcycle was not registered under Aduque's name. A show-cause order was issued to the rider and the registered owner.
Authorities also cited alleged traffic violations involving the motorcycle, including reckless driving, not wearing a standard helmet, and not having the required side mirrors.
Police said these violations could result in a 90-day suspension.
Analyn said she plans to pursue the case and offered a P10,000 reward for information that could lead to the suspect's arrest.
Other road rage incidents in Cebu
Another road rage incident happened in Barangay Kamputhaw, Cebu City, where a pickup truck driver was seen arguing with a motorcycle passenger before allegedly chasing him with a knife.
The Land Transportation Office Region 7 said the incident started after the pickup driver and a motorcycle taxi crossed paths.
According to the LTO, the pickup driver became angry after the motorcycle taxi allegedly cut him off. The driver later confronted the passenger, and the two argued.
The two sides later settled the matter at the barangay, and the case did not reach the police station. Both the motorcycle rider and the complainant declined to be interviewed.
The pickup driver, “James,” also declined an interview.

The LTO said James had been involved in another road incident on August 5, in the same area in Cebu City. A motorcycle rider identified as “Mark” said that James punched him twice after he overtook the pickup.

“Nag-overtake po ako. Tapos, nagalit siya nu’ng nag-overtake ako. Nakipagsagutan ako. Sobrang galit niya, sinuntok ako.” Mark said, adding that James later apologized and the two were discussing a settlement.
["I overtook him. Then he got angry when I did. I argued back. He was so furious that he hit me twice.”]
The LTO said a show-cause order had also been prepared in connection with the incident.
Motorcycle riders settle another Cebu dispute
Another road incident occurred in Barangay Malubog, Cebu City, where a group of motorcycle riders was seen attacking another rider.

The victim, Christopher, said he was traveling home on September 20 when he encountered the group. He said one motorcycle suddenly braked in front of him and another motorcycle hit him from behind, causing him to fall.
Christopher said he was punched after he got back on his motorcycle. He later lost consciousness during the confrontation.
The two sides later met at city hall and settled the dispute, according to Christopher.
“Humingi na sila ng tawad kahapon sa city hall namin. Naramdaman ko rin naman na totoo ‘yung paghihingi nila ng tawad kaya pinatawad ko na,” he said.
["They already apologized yesterday at our city hall. I felt that their apology was sincere, so I forgave them.”]
The group involved declined to comment, saying their lawyer advised them not to issue a statement because the matter had already been settled.
LTO: Some road rage incidents go unreported
LTO Region 7 said road rage incidents have become frequent, although many cases do not reach authorities or go viral online.

“We have at least one incident of road rage this month. Almost daily. Some of them go unreported. ‘Yan ‘yung problema. Hindi na reported. When you say kasi road rage, ‘yan na ‘yung dadaanan, sasampalin ‘yung side mirror, tapos tatakbo. That's already road rage. That is happening almost on a daily basis. However, very few lang ‘yung nagiging viral.”

["We have at least one road rage incident this month, in fact almost daily. Some of them go unreported, and that’s the problem. They aren't being reported anymore. Because when you talk about road rage, that includes someone passing by, hitting your side mirror, and driving off. That's already road rage, and it's happening almost on a daily basis. However, very few of those incidents actually go viral.”]

The 2016 killing of cyclist Mark Garalde by Army reservist Vhon Tanto was one of the country's most widely discussed road rage cases. Tanto was convicted of murder in 2019, three years after the incident. He was sentenced to reclusion perpetua and ordered to pay around P1.3 million in damages.
Garalde's family continues to keep the bicycle he was using when he was killed. A “ghost bike” installed by fellow cyclists as a memorial was removed in 2022.
His mother, Marilou, said she was grateful that the case resulted in a conviction.
Road rage cases and driver's license penalties
The LTO said road rage cases accounted for 26% of its cases beginning October 25, 2025, although the figure has since declined.
The agency said around 600 drivers have had their licenses suspended and more than 800 have had their licenses revoked over road rage incidents since October 2025.
The LTO urged motorists to avoid confrontations and remain calm while driving.

“Iwasan nila ang road rage. Marami na namatay sa road rage. Hindi perpekto ang kalye, maraming nangyayari, maging mahinahon tayo parati. Isipin natin ‘yung pamilya natin at trabaho natin. Umiwas tayo sa gulo.”

["They should avoid road rage. A lot of people have already died from road rage. The roads aren't perfect, and a lot of things can happen, so let's always stay calm. Let's think about our families and our jobs. Let's stay out of trouble."] —JCB, GMA News

articles.title: Lime bike profits double as rider numbers surge in England
articles.summary:
US-owned firm says average monthly users at its UK arm surged to 700,000 with sales up by a third

Love them or hate them, Lime ebikes are an increasingly common sight on England’s roads with…

blocks.text: Love them or hate them, Lime ebikes are an increasingly common sight on England’s roads with new figures showing annual profits more than doubling thanks to a surge in riders.

Lime’s average number of monthly users jumped 31% to approaching 700,000 as it added more than 4,500 ebikes and scooters to its fleet, taking the total to almost 38,000, the company’s UK arm said in accounts filed at Companies House.

Sales rose by a third to £148m in 2025 and profits more than doubled to £4.7m from £1.7m, as first reported by the Sunday Times. The progress followed expansion into new cities, including Oxford in 2024 and Nottingham in 2023, adding to its presence in London, Milton Keynes and Salford.

Despite the surge in trade, Lime’s UK accounts show it employed just 54 people in 2025, up from 39 a year before, largely because it relies on self-employed contractors to shift and service its ebikes and scooters.

The company, whose parent Neutron Holdings listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange last year valued at $1.7bn (£1.3bn), is part-owned by US ride-hailing app Uber. Lime was founded in 2017 in San Francisco, California, and now operates in about 230 cities across 29 countries, mostly in Europe.
At the time of the listing, Wayne Ting, the chief executive of Lime, said the company was having “conversations with lots of other [UK] municipalities”.

blocks.caption: Lime bikes have become almost ubiquitous in London. Photograph: Melanie Major/Alamy

blocks.text: The English devolution bill, passed in April, gives local authorities in England fresh powers to license rental ebike operators and set requirements around parking, safety and accessibility standards.
London’s transport body estimated in 2024 that one in 10 of the 1.5m daily cycle journeys in the capital are made on dockless ebikes such as Lime, Forest and Voi.
The schemes have fuelled a surge in cycling in London, helped by the patronage of celebrities such as Timothée Chalamet and most recently Kim Kardashian.

However, there have been mounting concerns about safety for riders and pedestrians. Rented bikes were reportedly responsible for almost a third of cyclist collisions with pedestrians that required police intervention.
Meanwhile, riders have been injured by defective bikes while cycling or suffered fractures caused by the weight of the bicycle falling on them, a phenomenon known as “Lime bike leg”.

Lime recently began introducing on the UK a new, smaller version of its electric bikes, with batteries repositioned towards the back wheel,after safety criticism. More than 1,500 of the new models are now in operation in England.
The company has said that more than 99.99% of Lime trips in London last year ended without a reported incident.
Charities representing blind residents and people with limited mobility have also raised concerns about the difficulty in navigating parts of London amid chaotic parking of rental bikes on pavements.

London boroughs have seized at least 3,000 ebikes this year, 2,000 of which were Lime bikes, a Guardian investigation found, as hire companies face growing calls to stop bicycles littering streets and blocking pavements.

articles.title: OpenAI pauses training of latest models after AI agents probed U.S. government sites in unexpected ways
articles.summary: OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.

image.caption: OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training 'only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards' in place. (Andrej Ivanov/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Business·New
OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.
No private info accessed but incidents were concerning enough to notify authorities

The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching U.S. federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.
Separately, AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a U.S. Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.

OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training "only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards" in place, adding that it expects it will have to "hit pause" again as AI develops and other issues emerge.

AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing non-public information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown, too.
OpenAI reveals unexpected AI activity on U.S. government websites
AI fears overblown, Trump says

It's the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyberattack targeting AI startup Hugging Face, a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control.

In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, U.S. President Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and co-ordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own.

items: China, U.S. agree to AI dialogue, tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods during Xi visit

blocks.text: The U.S. is not going to be "putting on brakes," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "They want to stop our progress because we're leading China by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way."
No private info accessed, reports
The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any non-public information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved.
In the Department of Education incident, OpenAI agents found API "developer keys" to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered.

In another case involving the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do.

items: OpenAI says its bots have interacted with multiple U.S. government sites in unexpected AI activity
Australia says OpenAI agent hacked government website

blocks.text: SEC spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said Saturday that "no nonpublic information was accessed."
The U.S. Department of Education said earlier that it found "no evidence of any impact to our website or databases."
Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a social media post Friday that the Hugging Face incident "is still the most severe event we've seen."
OpenAI previously shared six other reports of "unexpected or concerning" behaviour in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances.

articles.title: Redemption as John Cabang Tolentino hurdles to Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition where he placed fourth, John Cabang Tolentino bounces back with a season-best performance as he claims the men's 110m hurdles bronze in the Asian Games

blocks.text: PRIDE. John Cabang Tolentino in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition where he placed fourth, John Cabang Tolentino bounces back with a season-best performance as he claims the men's 110m hurdles bronze in the Asian Games
MANILA, Philippines – John Cabang Tolentino found redemption on Sunday, September 27, as he broke through for the Philippine athletics team at the 2026 Asian Games.
The 25-year-old Olympian clinched the bronze medal in the men’s 110m hurdles at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan.

Denied a spot on the podium in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, where he placed fourth, Tolentino bounced back and posted a season-best 13.48 seconds as he won the Philippines’ first athletics medal in this year’s Asian Games.
China’s Chen Yuanjiang clocked 13.15 seconds to capture the gold, while Japan’s Rachid Muratake bagged the silver with 13.29 seconds.
“I’m very happy. It was just a lot of self-pressure and I just did it,” said Tolentino, who was born to Filipino parents in Spain.
“Even in the hard times, I kept pushing … I was always dreaming about this.”
The Asian Games bronze adds to his collection, which includes a Southeast Asian Games gold and an Asian Indoor Athletics Championships bronze.
In December, Tolentino won the SEA Games title in record-breaking fashion in Bangkok, Thailand, shattering the previous mark that stood for a decade.
With an Asian Games medal in the bag, Tolentino eyes a second Olympic stint.
“I’m gonna go for LA Olympics,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Three in four UK GPs ‘too busy to talk to their patients in depth’
articles.summary:
Family doctors’ professional body finds the majority have no time to discuss preventative measures

A friendly chat with your GP about your life, health and happiness was once a key part of…

blocks.text: A friendly chat with your GP about your life, health and happiness was once a key part of the UK’s family doctor service.
But most GPs no longer have time to have pastoral conversations, because they are too busy dealing with the country’s rising tide of illness, research reveals.
Three out of four family doctors are now too time-pressed to talk to patients in depth about how they might stop smoking, lose weight or get more sleep, the Royal College of GPs has found.
Intense demands and ten-minute appointment slots mean they also miss opportunities to discuss taking more exercise with patients or review their medications to see if they still need to be on them.
The time to explore patients’ circumstances more fully and offer healthy living advice has been squeezed out of family doctors’ busy schedules, the head of the college said.

An RCGP survey of 2,316 GPs across the UK found that 75% had too little time to offer preventative healthcare, such as offering lifestyle advice and administering vaccinations. The results have raised concern about the government’s drive for the NHS – especially GPs – to do more to prevent people getting ill in the first place. One health expert called them alarming.

The college’s president, Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, who is a GP in east London, said: “General practice is dealing with enormous demand, so in a busy consultation we inevitably have to prioritise the problems that most need our attention that day.

“We will always act on symptoms or findings that need investigation or treatment. What can be squeezed out is the time to step back and look more holistically at how we can help that patient stay well in the long term.

“That might mean having a proper conversation with someone who smokes. We will of course advise patients about stopping smoking. But in a busy consultation there may not be enough time to explore in depth whether they want to stop, what has made it difficult in the past, what concerns they have and what support or treatment might work best for them.
“It is often the depth of those conversations, rather than simply identifying a risk and giving brief advice, that requires time.”

GPs already deliver important preventative care every day, she said. But “the reality is that when you’re working in a busy surgery, with a long list of patients to be seen, there isn’t always enough time in consultations to go beyond the issue a patient has come in for that day”.

The chief executive of the King’s Fund health thinktank, Sarah Woolnough, said: “With life expectancy in the UK among the lowest of most comparable countries, these findings are alarming as many GPs say they are too overwhelmed to carry out these important interventions, and may be missing conditions that could be treated earlier.
“GPs are often frustrated that the increasing demands for appointments mean they don’t have time to provide the holistic care they were trained for.”
after newsletter promotion
The RCGP makes clear in its report that the NHS needs to employ more GPs and ensure they have more time with patients in order to fulfil the prevention ambition.

The findings raise questions about ministers’ plan to make the NHS in England move “from sickness to prevention” in how it operates – one of the three “big shifts” outlined in the government’s ten-year health plan last year.
“Talk around shifting from sickness to prevention is meaningless if we cannot get these basics right first,” Woolnough said.

“If the government is serious on prevention, then more action is needed to support and enable GPs to consistently catch conditions and ill-health early, keeping people healthier for longer, and reducing pressures on wider NHS services down the line.”

A separate representative survey of 2,000 UK voters which the pollsters Censuswide undertook for the RCGP showed that 64% of the public trust family doctors to offer advice on healthy living. That was more than trust the NHS website (51%), pharmacists (38%), family and friends (22%), AI chatbots (7%) and social media influencers (5%).
The Department for Health and Social Care was approached for comment.

articles.title: Britain knew about the Holocaust as it happened. A new exhibition reckons with that truth
articles.summary:
Research draws upon reporting and witness testimony, while a permanent memorial is planned for London

The “complex and unsettling” story of what Britain knew during the Holocaust is being…

blocks.text: The “complex and unsettling” story of what Britain knew during the Holocaust is being explored amid plans to create a new permanent national memorial.

An exhibition highlighting how news of the atrocity reached Britain much earlier than is commonly understood will tour the country after being viewed privately by MPs at Portcullis House on the parliamentary estate at Westminster in September.

The research draws upon newspaper reporting, broadcasts, academic scholarship, witness testimony and government archives. The exhibition is a sample of a more extensive, permanent exhibition for the national Holocaust Memorial and Learning Centre, which is planned for a site in London.

blocks.caption: Adjaye Associates and Ron Arad won the design competition for the Holocaust memorial in London.

blocks.text: Martin Winstone, the senior historical adviser to the Holocaust Educational Trust, said: “There’s a feeling today that Britain really only found out about the Holocaust at the end of the war. But in 1942, the year in which most victims of the Holocaust were murdered, you couldn’t really escape this information in Britain. It was in every newspaper. It was on the BBC.

“The Manchester Guardian was the newspaper that reported most extensively on the Holocaust, taking a crusading position that there was more the British government and allied governments could be doing.”

For years, the Manchester Guardian, which was banned from Germany in 1933 for highlighting Adolf Hitler’s antisemitism, called for immigration restrictions to be lifted for Jews, lobbied for pressure to be applied to neutral nations to open their borders to refugees and for special rescue measures, realising that “the Nazis were aiming at the complete elimination of an entire group of people”.

Much of the information about the Holocaust, including the locations of death camps, was smuggled out of Poland – where the murders were “happening in plain sight” – by couriers to the London-based Polish government-in-exile.
Winstone said: “It was a challenging situation. There were lots of things the government had to deal with. And for much of that war, Britain was on the defensive.
“On one level, the government’s response was always, ‘we’ll win the war, that’s how we stop this’; while critics said, ‘there’ll be nobody left to save, if that’s what you’re waiting for’.”

During the second world war, the government commissioned reports on antisemitism in Britain, with agents opening people’s mail and recording conversations overheard in air raid shelters to gauge public opinion.

In what Winstone described as a “complex and unsettling story”, Ministry of Information bulletins revealed that while there was mass public sympathy for Jews in occupied Europe, it contended with anti-migration and antisemitic sentiment.

Winstone added: “Nearly everybody in Britain was disgusted about these mass murders, but at the same time you start getting more antisemitic discourse about Jews in Britain – that Jews were running the black market, avoiding military service and spreading panic.
“Even before the mass murder began, during the 1930s, there was a significant body of opinion which felt Britain should not be admitting refugees.”
after newsletter promotion

Winstone said UK immigration laws in the 1930s were highly restrictive, in part because of antisemitism earlier in the 20th century. But after the Kristallnacht pogrom of 1938, Britain relaxed restrictions to some extent, allowing Jewish children to come from Europe without visas. The Manchester Guardian reported how Jewish communities and Quakers in the city set up organisations to support refugees.
British women – from MP Eleanor Rathbone, to grassroots fundraisers and those who found themselves interned alongside Jews in France – were at the forefront of humanitarian efforts, Winstone said.

blocks.caption: The independent MP Eleanor Rathbone was at the forefront of humanitarian efforts.  Photograph: Hulton Deutsch/Corbis/Getty Images

blocks.text: A 2021 survey by Claims Conference found 21% of the British public knew the UK government was aware of the mass murder of Jews as early as 1941.

UK Holocaust Memorial Foundation is co-chaired by the broadcaster and former Labour politician Ed Balls and the Tory peer Eric Pickles, who said the exhibition would give an early insight into the work being developed for the forthcoming memorial.

The exhibition will be at the Northern Ireland assembly from 30 October until 13 November; the Scottish parliament from 7 to 10 December; before travelling to Cardiff from 16 January to 4 February 2027, coinciding with Holocaust Memorial Day on 27 January. It is also expected to visit Manchester, with a date and venue yet to be confirmed.

The UK Holocaust Memorial and Learning Centre, which would be at Victoria Tower Gardens, Westminster, does not have a confirmed opening date yet, as a planning application is being redetermined by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. The Holocaust Memorial Act 2026 received royal assent this year, granting legal clearance and government funding for the project.

articles.title: Datacenter developers accused of skirting key US pollution rules
articles.summary:
Firms manipulating process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental groups warn

Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting…

blocks.text: Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental advocates allege.

Companies need federal permits to emit a range of pollutants. In their permit applications, some in big tech are avoiding “major” reviews by dividing their emissions sources into separate, multiple “minor” sources that require less regulatory oversight, the advocates say.

This helps datacenters avoid public scrutiny, and permit applications are typically approved much faster. It also likely saves tech companies money, and avoids the hassle and cost of potential pollution controls, advocates say. Datacenters can be significant sources of nitrogen oxide, ozone, heavy metals, particulate matter, greenhouse gas and other dangerous air pollutants.

In North Carolina, Amazon and utility giant Duke Energy are installing 649 diesel generators to back up a new hyperscale center. They submitted two permits, and avoided a major review despite being in a low income area that already suffers from high levels of air pollution.

In New Mexico, the Project Jupiter datacenter developers attempted to circumvent a major review by proposing two natural gas “microgrids” for either side of the facility and submitting two “minor” permits. The overall project would have released enough pollution to trigger a major review.

In Frederick, Maryland, four datacenters with separate minor permits, including one by Amazon, operate on a single campus with a master developer, regulatory documents show. In other instances, data center developers have staggered minor permit requests over months that cumulatively emit as much pollution as a major source, advocates say.

These regulatory maneuvers make it less clear how much pollution residents living near the facilities are exposed to, and the move amounts to “lego permitting”, said Michael Koerber, a retired deputy director of the EPA’s Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards, which worked on permitting.

“They want to fly under the radar,” said Koerber, who now volunteers with the Environmental Protection Network nonprofit. “The more attention they have, the more difficult it gets to get the permit. They have consultants who are very good and know where the shortcuts are.”

Koerber noted that the situation is not unique to the data center industry. Cheryl Vetter, a former EPA employee who worked with Koeber and left the agency last year, said it was not common for data centers to use this tactic until after she left.
In a statement, an Amazon spokesperson said the company “appropriately applied for and obtained an air permit for our datacenter project”.

Under the Clean Air Act, companies building a project that will be a “major” source of air pollution, like some hyperscale data centers, are typically supposed to undergo a more stringent air emissions review. Among other protections, it is supposed to ensure that the pollution the facility would add to the local airshed would not violate air quality limits when combined with the air pollution already in the region.

This process can be lengthy, may require pre-construction monitoring, and, if the proposed data center is found to violate limits, may require companies to take steps to limit their pollution, like adding scrubbers to their smokestacks.

The Project Jupiter datacenter plans to divide its natural turbines into minor permits was “nothing short of preposterous”, attorneys with the New Mexico Environmental Law Center wrote in March comments submitted to state regulators. The firm is representing community members who would be impacted by the proposed plans’ pollution.

It in effect created a scenario in which one natural gas power plant would have operated with two minor permits, attorneys wrote. The permit application points to why the data center’s developers, Austin-based BorderPlex, attempted to do two permits.

The federal limit for a minor permit for hazardous air pollution is 25 tons per year. The project’s developers proposed releasing between 20.2 and 24.2 tons of hazardous air pollution from each of the grids, meaning that together they would have released as much as 44 tons of hazardous air pollution.

In regulatory documents, Maslyn Locke, an attorney working on the case, wrote that the “audacious attempt to arbitrarily distinguish two halves of the same source is insulting to both [regulators] and community members, as it is so clearly an attempt to avoid air pollution control requirements.”

The developer withdrew the application in April amid fierce community pushback, Locke said. The New Mexico environment department also opposed the proposal, a spokesperson told the Guardian. However, Locke told the Guardian there was no public evidence that regulators opposed it until now. New plans for the data center have been held up by the state supreme court over procedural problems, Locke said.

Vetter said the law allows for divided permits in some instances. Permits can be divided if two companies are polluting at the same location, but not if all the polluting activities are under common control. The sources must also be adjacent, though the definition of “adjacent” can include those that do not share a border, but operate as part of the same facility.

Amazon and Duke’s North Carolina plans call for nearly 250 tons per year of nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and volatile organic compounds. Amazon is proposing to emit about 98 tons of particulate matter annually, and 6.4 tons per year of hazardous air pollutants, including benzene and formaldehyde.

The heavily industrial region is already burdened by pollution from a Duke power plant and other plastic pellet factory, the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC) wrote in comments to North Carolina state regulators.

Heart disease, cancer, and respiratory disease are among the leading causes of death in the region, and the datacenter’s diesel generators’ particulate matter and hazardous pollutants will almost certainly increase those problems, advocates warn.

It appears the companies split the permits to avoid a major review, Kathleen Sullivan, a SELC attorney, told the Guardian. North Carolina regulators wrote that Duke’s generators are providing temporary power for about a year, and that Duke is operating them separately from Amazon’s generators. But the companies did not provide to regulators lease agreements and contracts, and some documents suggest Amazon controls all the generators, Sullivan alleged.
In its statement, Amazon said: “The separate permitting of Amazon’s and Duke’s respective projects reflects the actual ownership and operational structure.”
“They should be – and are – permitted under separate air permits,” the spokesperson said.

Even if some of the generators are only temporary, high levels of exposure to the dangerous pollutants for even an hour can cause health problems, and the plans should undergo more meaningful scrutiny, Sullivan added.
She said state regulators are “simply trusting two extremely wealthy and politically powerful companies without any verification”.

“North Carolina regulators failed to protect people’s health and the air we all breathe by blindly accepting the companies’ self-interested statements instead of doing their job to investigate the key facts,” Sullivan said.

blocks.text: Tennis·New
Canada's Leylah Fernandez captured her first title of the season with a 7-5, 6-0 win over Australia's Talia Gibson in the women's singles final at the Singapore Tennis Open on Sunday.
Laval, Que., native tops Australia's Talia Gibson in straight sets for 6th career title
The Laval, Que., native won the last nine games to secure the win in one hour 38 minutes. Fernandez dropped only one set across her five matches in the tournament.

articles.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
articles.summary: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

image.caption: The Vienna model has provided affordable housing to Viennese residents for more than 100 years Image: DW

blocks.text: In the European Union's most populous city, pressure on the housing market is so great that many of its residents are willing to undertake a historic experiment: Five years ago, Berliners voted in a referendum to instruct the Senate of the German capital to draft a law that would put an end to the power of large real estate companies. Those that owned more than 3,000 units should be expropriated, they said. The Senate did not act on the results of the referendum, which was non-binding. Meanwhile, the average cost of new leases has since risen by about half.

But in the Berlin elections on September 20, the socialist Left Party, which in its campaign had promised to act on the referendum, won the largest share of the vote. Whether it will be able to make good on its promises now depends on how negotiations to form a coalition shape up. But whatever happens, the election has drawn attention once again to the severity of the housing crisis in many cities across Europe.

blocks.caption: Left Party candidate Elif Eralp has promised to be a mayor for all Berliners. Her campaign was largely about providing affordable housing. Image: Britta Pedersen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Here are some initiatives that have already been put in place:
Vienna: The city is the landlord

The Vienna model is a flagship solution to soaring rent prices in Europe. The ambitious social housing program as introduced after World War I when the Austrian capital experienced a severe housing crisis. Beds were so scarce that some workers had to sleep in shifts. Diseases such as tuberculosis spread in the cramped living conditions.

The model serves to stabilize the city's housing market to this day: According to the Vienna authorities, the city owns approximately 220,000 municipal apartments that it rents out as well as 200,000 subsidized dwellings. More than 60% of Vienna's residents live in one of these two types of housing. This also helps to stabilize prices on the private market.
Public funds in Vienna keep rents down
Basel: Public land, private buildings

The fact that housing is becoming increasingly expensive in many cities is largely due to the fact that a city's attractiveness is reflected in land prices. In many places, people are considering how to decouple rents from the price of land. One means of doing this is not to sell municipal land but to lease it to cooperatives or socially-conscious investors. This benefits councils that do not have to bear construction costs and developers too, as they do not have to factor in exorbitant land costs that are ultimately passed on to tenants.

The Swiss city of Basel is one of the pioneers of this model. About 40% of all cooperative housing units are located on public land. The Spanish city of Barcelona and the Portuguese capital Lisbon have also stepped up efforts to put this model in place.
Paris: Buying back office buildings and converting them into homes

It is harder if land and buildings are in private hands. In 2014, the French capital Paris launched an anti-displacement plan giving the municipality a "first right of refusal" in gentrifying neighborhoods to increase the share of affordable housing in the city. The current target is 30% social housing for low-income residents by 2035

Earlier this year, the French government and the Paris regional authorities identified 61 projects that could convert empty office buildings into housing and create up to 8,200 homes in the inner suburbs of the French capital.

blocks.caption: Certain office buildings in the Paris suburbs are being converted into affordable homes Image: Vincent Isore/IP3press/imago images

blocks.text: Prague: Apartments for public-sector workers

The Czech capital has found another way to keep those without whom the city could not function in Prague: caregivers, police officers, teachers and sanitation workers. Some 660 new energy-efficient apartments reserved specifically for public-sector employees have just been built.

The subsidiary of a Czech bank, which has received European loans, handled the development. The aim is to keep rents 20% below the market rate thanks to economies of scale, and it is not the bank who decides on the tenants but hospitals or public sector agencies, which draw up leases and can attract new employees with affordable rent options. More apartments are currently being planned.

blocks.caption: Few people can afford to live in the center of PragueImage: Eva Korinkova/REUTERS

blocks.text: Dublin: Non-profit cost rental housing

It has also become difficult for people with low incomes to stay in the Irish capital Dublin. During and after Ireland's financial crisis of 2008, foreign investors bought up a lot of real estate and at the same time rents skyrocketed when several major tech companies chose Dublin as their EU headquarters because of favorable tax rates. There are now long waiting lists for public housing in the city whose supply remains too low.

In 2021, the Irish government introduced the Cost Rental Housing program to provide housing to those on middle incomes, i.e. those who earn too much to qualify for public housing but too little to have a chance on the private market. To qualify in Dublin, a household has to have a net income of below €66,000 ($75,000) per year. Non-profits or public agencies lease out the apartments and rents are below market levels, by an average of almost 30% according to a recent study by the Dublin-based Economic & Social Research Institute (ESRI).

The Irish government hopes to be able to deliver 18,000 low-cost rental homes by the end of the decade. Last year, there were more than 4,200 applicants for 104 apartments in a new community in a suburb of Dublin.
This article was translated from German.
Berlin has space, so why is housing so expensive?

articles.title: ‘Police were banging on the door’: villagers near RAF Fairford describe evacuation
articles.summary:
Local people say members of WhatsApp group noticed suspicious activity around vans in Whelford overnight

Those living near RAF Fairford have been used to disturbance from protesters and a…

blocks.text: Those living near RAF Fairford have been used to disturbance from protesters and a heavy police presence after the decision to allow the US air force to use it as a base for attacks on Iran.
But in recent weeks, people have noticed dramatically increased security measures, with the gates of the base newly barricaded.
“In the prior few weeks they have put heavy, very heavy vehicles across all gates,” one person said.
She described them as “very big tractors and things like that” parked behind gates into the base, adding: “So obviously they’re taking security seriously.”
The resident said “great big concrete walls” had also been placed behind some gates, including on Dunfield Loop and Whelford Road.

If local people had questioned the necessity of those steps, they may have been persuaded this weekend. In the very early hours of Sunday morning, some in the nearby village of Whelford noticed suspicious activity around three vans parked there. The local WhatsApp group lit up with messages from people wondering what to do about the vehicles blocking a lane in the village.

One resident of Whelford, named Jason, who declined to give his surname, said they were first aware something was happening overnight at about 1.30am, when people on the chat group started discussing the vans.

blocks.caption: A Tesco grocery delivery vehicle is stopped at a roadblock in Fairford. Photograph: Getty Images

blocks.text: Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said one person had reported three “suspicious vans” in the village in the early hours of Sunday morning.
“Evidently, they phoned the airbase police, who didn’t answer the phone,” he said. “It just rang out, so she dialled 999.”
Residents were then woken at 6am by police banging on their door and telling them to leave immediately. They were taken to a nearby leisure centre.
Tudsbery added: “[The police] were then banging on the door, so I went downstairs in my dressing gown.
“There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there’s been a major incident, said he couldn’t elaborate.”
Police then announced that several men had been arrested for explosives offences.
Thirty emergency vehicles were seen in the village, with the army, a bomb squad and counter-terrorism police all investigating at the scene. Explosives experts were seen examining the three vans.

The RAF base has come to prominence since March, and the beginning of the US-Israeli war with Iran. From the perimeter of the RAF base it has been possible to see heavy bombs being loaded on to American aircraft.

Fairford has a particularly long runway, which extends almost 2 miles (3km). It is reinforced to support heavy bombers such as the B-1 and B-52, which have been deployed in attacks on Iran. The aircraft are capable of carrying large payloads, including “bunker buster” bombs.
Jason, 50, was evacuated to Cirencester leisure centre at 6am on Sunday with his family and 11-week-old puppy, Poppy, and friends who were visiting from London.
“We went to bed,” he said. “It was early the next morning when the doorbell rang. It was the police, asking residents to evacuate as there had been a major incident.”

Jason, who works in consulting, said earlier on Sunday there were about 40 to 50 people in the leisure centre, ranging from toddlers to elderly villagers, as well as a number of dogs. He said they had been given no more details than those that had been released publicly by police.
It was unclear when people would be able to go back to their normal lives; those at the leisure centre said they had been asked by authorities if they had anywhere else to stay on Sunday night.
By Sunday afternoon, the cordon around the village expanded so no one could get anywhere near it. Tudsbery said he hoped he could get home soon: he had left his cat, Misty, behind.

articles.title: PH, US mark 80 years of partnership with new booklet
articles.summary: The Philippines and the United States have marked 80 years of partnership in business, diplomacy and people-to-people ties with the launch of a new edition of a booklet highlighting the countries'…

blocks.text: The Philippines and the United States have marked 80 years of partnership in business, diplomacy and people-to-people ties with the launch of a new edition of a booklet highlighting the countries' longstanding relationship.

The second edition of the booklet, “The Philippines Matters for America, America Matters for the Philippines,” commemorates eight decades of diplomatic relations between the two countries, which were established on July 4, 1946.
The first edition of the booklet was published in 2022.

A project led by the US East-West Center, an education and research organization, the booklet supposedly highlights the alliance, trade, investment, educational exchanges, partnerships and supply chains between the two countries.

During his speech, US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton underscored the strong relationship between the Philippines and the US and expressed confidence in its continued growth in the years ahead.
Among the areas of Philippine-US partnership highlighted by Lipton were the Luzon Economic Corridor, Pax Silica, artificial intelligence and nuclear energy.
“Our countries share an incredible, incredible history together. We're here to take our relationship to the next level,” Lipton said on Thursday.

Meanwhile, Department of Foreign Affairs Undersecretary Maria Andrelita Austria described the launch of the booklet as a “very strategic and timely” initiative as it coincides with the anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Philippines and the US.

“On July 4, 1946, the Philippines and the United States formally opened a new chapter in our shared history. It was a moment that started not only the recognition of Philippine independence, but also the beginning of a strong diplomatic partnership between two sovereign nations bound by history, democratic values and enduring people-to-people ties,” Austria said.

“Eighty years later, the relationship remains one of the Philippines' most important and deeply valued partnerships. Let me take this opportunity to highlight the top impacts and figures which underscore the depth and breadth of our alliance,” she added.
The booklet noted that bilateral trade between the two countries reached $41.7 billion in 2025, representing a 13% increase from 2024.
The United States is also the Philippines' top single-country trading partner for agricultural products, supplying 15% of its agricultural imports and buying 18% of its agricultural exports in 2025.
The booklet further indicated that US foreign direct investment (FDI) in the Philippines totaled $6 billion, while Philippine FDI in the US amounted to $532 million.
It also showed the number of jobs generated and supported through investments by the two countries, as well as the foreign assistance and health cooperation provided by the US to the Philippines.
Based on the booklet, exports to the Philippines supported 65,400 US jobs in 2024, the majority of which were in California, Texas and Washington.
Since 1949, US assistance to the Philippines has focused on economic development, peace and security, and health.

As of June 2025, the US had provided health assistance funding for global health security, tuberculosis, maternal and child health, neglected tropical diseases, integrated supply chains, nutrition and HIV/AIDS.
The booklet also highlighted Filipino medical workers, noting that they make up 5% of the nursing workforce and 3% of the healthcare workforce in the US.
The Philippines is also the top country of origin for immigrant healthcare professionals in the US, with Filipino immigrants comprising 12% of all foreign-born US healthcare workers.

The booklet also presented figures on income generated by Filipino visitors to the US, as well as the Filipino population, Filipino Americans in elected office and cultural connections between the two countries.
It said Filipinos make up 18% of the Asian American population in the United States, with an estimated 4.6 million people.
California, Hawaii, Texas, Washington and Nevada have the largest Filipino American populations.
Filipino Americans in Hawaii also have a strong political presence, with around 15% of state representatives and 24% of state senators being of Filipino descent.
From 2024 to 2025, there were 4,573 students from the Philippines studying in higher education institutions in the US.
Meanwhile, 326 American students studied in the Philippines from 2023 to 2024.
In terms of travel and tourism, the booklet showed that 1.1 million Americans visited the Philippines, while 315,000 Filipinos visited the US in 2025.
The US also earned $2 billion from Filipino tourist spending in 2024. Most Filipino visitors traveled to California, Florida and New York.
The year 2026 also marks the 75th anniversary of the Mutual Defense Treaty between the Philippines and the US, as well as the 250th anniversary of US independence.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: UK: 5 arrested after 'major incident' near Fairford air base
articles.summary: Scores of homes were evacuated in the UK town of Whelford, near an air base used by the US military, with bomb disposal teams checking "suspicious vehicles" at the scene. Police said five men had…

image.caption: The US Air Force has used the British base for attacks against IranImage: Toby Shepheard/REUTERS

blocks.text: British authorities evacuated buildings and deployed military bomb disposal teams over a "major incident" in the town of Whelford on Sunday morning.
The town is located near the Fairford air base, which is used by the US military. Around 30 emergency vehicles were seen in the area, including police cars, ambulances, and fire engines.
Counter-terrorism police were leading the investigation. On Sunday afternoon, London's Metropolitan police said five men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a "terrorist act."

blocks.caption: UK police blocked roads leading to the Fairford air baseImage: Toby Shepheard/REUTERS

blocks.text: Previously, the authorities said that several men were "arrested on suspicion of offences the ​Explosives Act."
"A cordon is currently in place but we'd like to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained," British police said.
Bomb disposal units examining three 'suspicious vehicles'
Separately, local police said they had received a call earlier on Sunday about "three suspicious vehicles" heading to the base.
"Armed officers responded and subsequently arrested five men in the Whelford area," assistant chief constable Richard Ocone told reporters.
He added that a cordon of 400 meters, or approximately 1/4 of a mile, has been put in place around the vehicles "while the army's explosive ordinance disposal unit examine them."
"As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations take place," Ocone said.
He added that some of the evacuees were taken to a nearby leisure center.
The Gloucestershire police representative also asked the public "not to speculate" but follow official channels instead.
Officials stay tight-lipped

A spokesperson for ​the US Air Force refused to discuss specific steps when contacted by the Reuters news agency, saying only that both US and British forces "remain vigilant and will take ⁠appropriate ​actions to ensure the safety and security of our ​US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families."

blocks.caption: This Fairford base gates was blocked by construction machinery Image: Toby Shepheard/REUTERS

blocks.text: The background for the incident was not immediately clear.

The UK has allowed the US to use Fairford for its war against Iran, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards warning UK officials against the move this summer. The evacuations also come at a time of heightened tensions in Northern Ireland, and less than two months after Germany discovered an explosive-laden drone at the Leipzig airport, which its authorities attributed to Russia.

articles.title: Two giant pandas set off to Atlanta zoo from China after Xi-Trump summit
articles.summary:
Pandas departed Chengdu for their new homes in Georgia as part of agreement between Chinese and US governments

Two giant pandas departed Chengdu in south-western

blocks.text: Two giant pandas departed Chengdu in south-western China early on Sunday for their new homes in Atlanta, Georgia, as part of an agreement between the Chinese and US governments.

While in Washington DC for a three-day summit with Donald Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping announced that the pandas would arrive in Atlanta in the coming days. The loan of the pandas to the Atlanta zoo was one of the few concrete outcomes to come out of Xi’s state visit with the US president, which saw expressions of goodwill between the leaders, but no fixes to any of the longstanding differences between the two countries.
Atlanta said farewell to its last pandas in 2024, leaving the zoo without the bears. The new agreement was announced back in April, but without any dates.

Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are the two adult pandas that will be on loan to Zoo Atlanta for 10 years as part of the agreement. Both pandas were born in 2020 and were kept at the Chengdu research base of giant panda breeding. Ping Ping, the male, has dark black circles around his eyes, while Fu Shuang, the female, has a forehead that protrudes a bit, according to the Xinhua News Agency.
China has long used the pandas as part of its diplomacy globally, deploying the bears in loan programs as expressions of goodwill and letting loan agreements lapse when tensions arise.
Xi had said the loan program was an example of “friendship between the Chinese and Americans”.

articles.title: ‘I wanted to help another family’: four surrogates on how they feel about the surrogacy discourse
articles.summary:
The Guardian spoke with surrogates across the US about what they think of the controversy surrounding the practice

Surrogacy has been thrust into the national spotlight in recent weeks, with…

blocks.text: Surrogacy has been thrust into the national spotlight in recent weeks, with both the announcement of Lena Dunham using a surrogate to start a family and the ongoing legal battle surrounding McKenna West, a gestational surrogate who fled to Texas to avoid having an abortion that was requested by the child’s biological parents.

With a renewed public interest on commercial, or compensated, surrogacy, the Guardian spoke with surrogates across the US who shared their experiences and how they feel about surrogacy being part of a global, public conversation.

Liggia Spicer, a 34-year-old woman based in upstate New York, first considered getting involved with surrogacy work after hearing about a mutual friend who was looking into using a surrogate after battling cancer and undergoing a hysterectomy.
“I probably did about two years of research before I turned to my husband and was like: ‘OK I think I want to do this,’” she said.

Spicer ended up working with an agency, ConceiveAbilities, where she was matched with a couple after what she described as a “vigorous” screening process that included a background check, financial check, psychological screen and a review of previous labor and delivery history. Most surrogacy programs require that a woman has given birth previously before becoming a surrogate.

ConceiveAbilities provided her with an attorney to assist with the creation of a surrogacy contract, an agreement that comes to pass before an embryo transfer and details the rights of the surrogate and the intended parents. It also addresses insurance, payment of medical bills, liability for medical complications and the intended parents’ presence during doctor’s visits and at delivery.

Notably, West’s case has brought up questions of how much bodily autonomy carriers are afforded in surrogacy. West violated her surrogacy contract by refusing to get an abortion after the fetus she was carrying was discovered to have a congenital heart defect. She later fled to Texas, where abortion is banned, and gave birth to the child. West has sought conservatorship over the child as well, which would give her a say in the child’s medical treatment. The US supreme court has declined to intervene in the case.

blocks.caption: McKenna West, left, arrivers with her legal team for a court hearing in Dallas, Texas, on 25 August 2026. Photograph: LM Otero/AP

blocks.text: “As surrogates, we do things that we may not do in our own pregnancies, but at the end of the day, it’s not our child,” Spicer said. “As long as what we’re being asked is safe to do.”

Kristy Miller, a 38-year-old, two-time surrogate based in Indianapolis, also worked with ConceiveAbilities. She spoke of the requests that a surrogate can make when being matched with intended parents.

“I remember feeling very strongly that I wanted there to be a trusting relationship [with the intended parents],” she said. “I didn’t want to feel micromanaged. I didn’t want someone to be kind of dictating what I ate every day, or how I took care of myself.”
Critics of surrogacy also argue that the process treats women’s bodies as a commodity.

Under Vogue’s Instagram post announcing Dunham’s essay about her surrogate journey, one commenter wrote: “Let’s not normalize buying humans.” Another said: “The concept of rich people renting poor people’s wombs will never not be strange.”

Dunham has spoken publicly about her fertility issues for years and writes about them at length in her 2026 book, Famesick. Her struggles have included an Ehlers-Danlos syndrome diagnosis, nearly two decades of advanced endometriosis and a total hysterectomy at 31 years old.
Spicer said: “It’s important that everyone should decide what happens to their body, and I wanted to get pregnant to help another family.
“That’s my decision,” she added. She now works as a surrogate engagement coordinator at ConceiveAbilities.

Christine S, a 38-year-old former gestational surrogate in New York state, carried and gave birth to a child for a same-sex male couple in 2025 with New York Surrogacy Center. Christine, who declined to share her last name for privacy reasons, said she understands concerns about reproductive exploitation, but believes that opponents of commercial surrogacy haven’t been informed enough on the intricacies of the process in the US.

“I think it’s just [that] they don’t understand enough about it,” she said. “Because there are situations where there are women that are held against their will to breed, right? Like that is a legit concern. But I volunteered. I didn’t do this against my will.

“And the journey of working with someone to be a surrogate, not only is it costly, but I also feel like [intended parents are] offering somebody an opportunity too. I had a job for a temporary amount of time, and it was a high-risk job, but it was also a high reward.”

Christine received $45,000 for carrying the child, in addition to coverage for her medical and legal fees. Spicer was paid $67,000, which was broken down and paid out over the course of the pregnancy.

Kimber Alston, a 36-year-old gestational surrogate based in Texas, is pregnant with her fifth surrogate child, and in the middle of her ninth pregnancy overall. Her first experience as a surrogate was in 2018 for a same-sex male couple in Italy. Since then, she has embarked on surrogate journeys both independently and with agencies, and given birth to children who live in Paris and Mexico, among other cities around the world.
She said she has formed close bonds with the intended parents she’s worked with, and frequently receives pictures and videos of the children she carried.

“What keeps me going is being able to help people have something that they couldn’t have otherwise,” she said. Alston, who also now works for a surrogacy agency she previously used, said that interacting with intended parents reminds her why has chosen to be a surrogate multiple times.

“I watch these couples every day come in and tell their stories; I’m in these match calls and watching them cry and not be able to have a child of their own,” she said. “I’m like: ‘If I could do it just one more time, I might as well just do it.’”
Multiple surrogates said the biggest misconception they see is the notion that surrogates get attached to the baby they are carrying, and may refuse to give the child up after delivery.

“I have never known a surrogate who felt like ‘mom’ to the baby [they were] carrying,” said Miller. “I think it’s hard for people to wrap their head around that unless they are truly considering [surrogacy].”
Spicer emphasized the need for levity throughout the experience.

“Honestly, I tell a lot of girls who want to be surrogates: ‘You have to have a sense of humor. You have to just take things on the chin and laugh it off,’” she said. “You could tell them until you’re blue in the face: ‘I’m not attached to this baby,’ and they still just don’t understand.”

articles.title: Marcos expresses gratitude for greetings on his 69th birthday
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Sunday thanked those who greeted him on his 69th birthday on September 13, 2026.

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 8:47pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Sunday thanked those who greeted him on his 69th birthday on September 13, 2026.

“Maraming salamat sa lahat ng bumati sa aking kaarawan noong nakaraang linggo. Hindi na rin ako halos nagkaroon ng oras mag-celebrate kasama ng buong pamilya dahil dire-diretso na ang schedule mula Ilocos hanggang sa India,” Marcos said in a Facebook video.
(Thank you very much to everyone who sent their birthday wishes last week. I barely had time to celebrate with my entire family because of my packed schedule from Ilocos all the way to India.)
Marcos spent his birthday in New Delhi, India, where he was invited to participate in the 18th BRICS Summit as an outreach participant and in his capacity as 2026 ASEAN chair.
Salo-salo sa Palasyo
Similar to last year’s celebration, Marcos hosted a “Salo-Salo sa Palasyo,” opening Malacañang to the public for a special program and festivities.
More than 98 local government units from across the country attended the gathering, according to Marcos.
“Bawat frontline service agency ng gobyerno kasama, kaya parang isang malaking selebrasyon na rin ang naganap,” he said.
(Every frontline government service agency was represented, turning it into one big celebration.)
As part of the celebration, relief aid was also distributed to attendees, Marcos said.
Outreach
In his message, Marcos highlighted the expanded Zero-Balance Billing initiative launched in line with his birthday celebration.

While the Zero-Balance Billing program typically covers only ward patients, Marcos said a special exception was made at around 132 hospitals nationwide, allowing all patients to have their medical bills covered.
“Normally, mga ward patients lang ang kasama dito, pero noong araw na ‘yon nilahat na natin. Basta nasa ospital ka, anumang kwarto, bayad na ang bill ninyo,” Marcos said.
(Normally, this program only applies to ward patients, but on that day, we covered everyone. As long as you were in the hospital, regardless of the room type, your bill was paid.)
“Humigit-kumulang 132 hospitals ang kabilang dito mula sa Luzon, Visayas at Mindanao. ‘Yung iba sa kanila ay umabot na sa milyon ang hospital bill—bayad na ‘yan,” he added.
(Around 132 hospitals took part in the initiative across Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao. Some patients had hospital bills reaching millions of pesos, and those bills have already been paid.)
Aside from hospital assistance, Marcos said outreach initiatives were also conducted in communities and schools, providing medical checkups, free medicines and other forms of aid.
According to Marcos, the initiatives benefited around 175,565 individuals across roughly 282 participating sites. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Ten climbers missing after avalanche hits Himalayan base camp
articles.summary: The Nepali team was preparing to take overseas climbers up the Himlung Himal peak.

blocks.text: At least 10 Nepali climbers who were preparing to lead an expedition are missing after an avalanche hit a base camp in the Himalayas on Sunday.
The climb's organisers said the local guides were at a staging point close to the Himlung Himal peak in Manang district when the avalanche struck on Sunday morning.
Forecasts showed there was heavy snowfall around the 7,126 metre (23,380ft) peak in recent days, which lies on Nepal's border with Tibet.
Poor weather has hampered rescue efforts, with helicopters and rescue teams unable to reach the site.
Bibhuti Chand Thakur, of Himalaya Holidays Trekking, told AFP news agency: "Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing."
The Nepali team had been sent ahead of foreign climbers to prepare the camp, manage the route and fix ropes on the mountain.
Nepal's mountain districts have seen persistent rain and snow in recent days, creating treacherous conditions for the country's economically important climbing tourism industry.
Climbers were forced to leave Mount Manaslu, the eighth highest peak in the world, earlier this week due to the rising threat of avalanches.
The latest death of Nepali climbers comes less than two months after six lost their lives on Broad Peak in Pakistan, including renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja.
Extreme weather further south in the neighbouring Indian region of Uttar Pradesh has killed more than 50 people, officials there said.
It comes as efforts to recover bodies continues on the Nepal-Tibet border, where more than 6,000 people are still missing after a massive flood and landslide in August.

More than 1,400 people are confirmed to have died after a glacial collapse in the Himalayas sent vast quantities of water and debris careering down the Trishuli River valley, sweeping away settlements.

image.caption: Canada's Jonathan David plays a pass during a 1-0 win over Chile in an international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto on Saturday night. (Chris Young/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Soccer·Recap
The Canadian men's soccer team kicked off a new four-year cycle in style Saturday night with a 1-0 win over Chile in a chippy international friendly at BMO Field in Toronto.
1st game for host side since falling to Morocco in World Cup Round of 16
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Sep 27, 2026 8:26 AM EDT | Last Updated: 20 minutes ago

It was the first game for the host side since falling to Morocco in the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup. Jonathan David scored the lone goal in front of a crowd of 23,310 and Dayne St. Clair earned the clean sheet.
"We wanted to come back here in Toronto after the World Cup to say thank you to the fans," said Canadian midfielder Mathieu Choiniere. "I think that's the best way that we did it - by a win."

The Canadian lineup was missing some key players for the first of three friendlies over the next fortnight. Captain Alphonso Davies (honeymoon), defender Derek Cornelius (hip) and goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau (personal) were unavailable.

David wore the captain's armband for 30th-ranked Canada. He was joined up top by Cyle Larin, who scored in the Canadian team's first World Cup game here on June 12, a 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina.
Canadian men's soccer team defeats Chile in international friendly
"It felt amazing," Larin said. "I think I felt the same type of energy and we started off fast in the game and we were able to get one early.
"So it was amazing to be back and to get that feeling back at BMO."
The match billed as "The Homecoming" began with a ceremony to honour the World Cup squad, which qualified for the knockout stage for the first time and beat South Africa in the Round of 32.
Chile, the world No. 49, did not qualify for the World Cup. The South American country's last appearance in the tournament came in 2014.
Canada was on the front foot early and was rewarded when David tallied in the 12th minute.

Ralph Priso started the play with a long ball to winger Jacob Shaffelburg, who found Larin with a cross. Goalkeeper Christian Bravo stopped Larin's initial shot but the rebound floated across the goalmouth and David tapped it in with his left foot.
David raised a No. 13 Cornelius jersey in the air as he returned to the sideline. Cornelius was hurt during a training session earlier in the week.
"I'm always expecting to score every game," David said. "So I asked them for it to be prepared."

items: Canadian men's soccer coach Marsch says team hopes to crack top 24 in world rankings

blocks.text: Chilean midfielder Lucas Cepeda was shown a red card in the 35th minute after getting tangled up with Canadian defender Richie Laryea.

As Cepeda was pulled down, his leg came upward and his boot caught Laryea on the side of the head. The contact drew blood near the eyebrow but Laryea stayed in the game after receiving medical attention.

Canada caught a break moments later when Niko Sigur was knocked down and St. Clair was caught out of the area. Chile's Jonathan Villagra had a chance to hit the ball into the empty net from distance but he put it over the bar.
Chile was down to nine men just four minutes into the second half.
Gabriel Suazo got the red after he was shown a second yellow card. His forearm caught Sigur in the head as they jumped for a ball.
Canada pressed with the two-man advantage but the Chilean backline held firm.
Jovan Ivanisevic made his national men's team debut as a wave of substitutes came on in the 62nd minute.
Hoilett makes final appearance
Junior Hoilett, in his final appearance with the squad, subbed in in the 76th minute. He was honoured for his 11-year run with the national team after the game.
"I was emotional, man," Hoilett said. "I was trying to hold it together when I first stepped on the field. It was a special moment."
A Laryea strike from distance in the 84th minute hit the post. Richard Chukwu made his national men's team debut in the 88th minute.
Head coach Jesse Marsch said Canada has set a long-term goal of reaching the top 24 in the world rankings as it looks to qualify for the 2030 World Cup in Portugal, Morocco and Spain.
Next up is an Oct. 3 friendly in Montreal against No. 50 Peru. Canada will visit the 16th-ranked United States on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minn.

articles.title: Bagunas rues Alas’ lack of support in Asian Games; PNVF apologizes
articles.summary: Bryan Bagunas reveals Alas Pilipinas players have not received their allowances since July, forcing some to miss practices during their Asian Games buildup due to financial constraints

blocks.text: SOAR. Bryan Bagunas in action for Alas Pilipinas Men in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Bryan Bagunas reveals Alas Pilipinas players have not received their allowances since July, forcing some to miss practices during their Asian Games buildup due to financial constraints

MANILA, Philippines – Alas Pilipinas Men team captain Bryan Bagunas rued the lack of financial support in the lead-up to and during the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, revealing that some players were forced to borrow money just to attend training.
xBagunas voiced his frustration after the Philippines’ 25-16, 27-25, 25-22 tournament-opening loss to South Korea on Sunday, September 27.
The star outside spiker said the players have not received their allowances since July, forcing some to miss practices during their Asian Games buildup due to financial constraints.

“Regarding our allowance, even some of the players borrowed money from our teammates or other people just so they could get to training and travel back home. It was really tough for us to practice every day. Sometimes, we’re only seven or eight in training. It was really difficult,” said Bagunas in Filipino.
“I understand because most of the players are student-athletes. We just helped each other out so we could have complete attendance in practice.”
Although the Philippine Sports Commission provided allowances to the athletes, Bagunas said Alas Men players still have to pay for expenses out of their own pockets.
For instance, Bagunas and his teammates sometimes have to buy their own meals because the serving hours at their hotel often clashed with their training sessions.
“It is really disheartening because we’re representing the country. We do not feel the support that we deserve,” said Bagunas.

All Bagunas could do is encourage his teammates as Alas Men focuses on the task at hand, with matches against China and Chinese Taipei in Group D coming up on Monday, September 28, and Tuesday, September 29, respectively.
The Philippines needs a top-two finish in the group to advance to the quarterfinals.
“I just motivate them to keep fighting. Hopefully, we’ll get better support in the future,” Bagunas said.

The Philippine National Volleyball Federation apologized on Sunday following Bagunas’ remarks and explained its side, saying it continues to deal with “substantial financial liabilities and outstanding obligations” that the new administration headed by president Frank Lao inherited.

“We acknowledge the concerns raised by Mr. Bagunas in his recent interview. We recognize the sacrifices our athletes have made, including having to shoulder their own expenses and, in some instances, borrow money. This is a situation that no National Athlete should ever have to endure,” the PNVF said in a statement.
The PNVF also said that Lao gave Alas Men allowances and has advanced funds to address concerns raised by the teams competing in the quadrennial showpiece.

“Our national athletes deserve a federation that works just as hard for them as they battle for our country. Our athletes deserve better. Philippine volleyball deserves better. And we will work tirelessly to deliver better,” the PNVF said. – Rappler.com
